newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SAS attacks Estonia air row stance.
newsitem.headline: SAS attacks Estonia air row stance.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines, locked in a dispute with Estonia over flights between Tallinn, Stockholm and Copenhagen, said the Estonian side's stance was unacceptable and confirmed that flights may be suspended.
Estonia wants SAS to cut its flights on the Tallinn-Copenhagen route to one a day from two and has refused to allow it to fly twice a day to Stockholm.
"Scandinavia is recognised as an aviation unit by all our partner countries and Estonia is the first exception," SAS said in a statement.
"This is unacceptable for the Scandinavian side."

SAS argues that the routes should be treated as one issue and that it and Estonian Air, majority-owned by Danish Maersk, itself owned by A.P. Moeller, should have three flights a day between Scandinavia and Estonia.
The Estonians say that the two routes are separate issues and that there is currently too much capacity.
SAS confirmed remarks by the Estonian Civil Aviation Authority that the row may result in flights being suspended.
"As the parties could find no solution there is no approved flight plan between Estonia, Denmark and Sweden," it said.
"This means that if a last minute solution cannot be found, there is a danger that air traffic between Scandinavia and Estonia will stop."
A solution has to be found by November 15, when the winter schedule is due to come into force.
SAS said that the Estonians were interpreting aviation agreements differently than before although they had been in place since 1992.
"Now the Estonian side wants to achieve a strict 50/50 capacity ratio on these routes and also to decide SAS's timetable," the statement added.
